FROM: Giselle M. Hernandez, Marketing and Community Engagement Manager

SUBJECT: City update on the Tweedy Mile Complete Streets Project

PURPOSE: Staff will provide an update on the Tweedy Mile Complete Streets Project.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file.

BACKGROUND: The City of South Gate will implement the Tweedy Mile Complete Streets Project to
enhance safety and mobility in the community. This project is a multi-million dollar investment that aims
to meet the needs of residents by enhancing pedestrian, bicycle and motorist safety, improving pavement
conditions, and beautifying Tweedy Boulevard between Dearborn Avenue and Dorothy Avenue. Funded
with local and federal grant funds, the project will include several pedestrian improvements like curb
extensions, curb ramps, parklets, new street furniture, pedestrian related trac signal improvements, and
pavement rehabilitation along the Tweedy Boulevard corridor.

City staff will present the proposed improvements and be available to answer questions from the public.

1
UPDATE ON THE SHOP
LOCAL DIGITAL GIFT
CARD PROGRAM  The Tweedy Mile Advisory Board received and filed the City's update on
  the Shop Local Digital Gift Card Program by motion of Vice Chair Varas
  and seconded by Board Member Masushige.

  Acting Management Analyst Mares explained to the Board that the City
  Council approved $15,000 in ARPA funds for the purpose of supporting
  local businesses in the city of South Gate. She encourages everyone to
  participate in the Gift Card Program because not only is it helping our
  local businesses, but the consumers are able to benefit from using the gift
  cards. Extra funding will be applied to those participating depending on
  the amount of funds placed in the gift card.

  Board Member Masushige asked if the gift card had an expiration date.

  Ms. Mares explained that the gift cards have a year expiration date.

  Board Member Masushige asked when the program launched.

  Ms. Mares explained that this program was launched on February 14,
  2023. There are twenty merchants, and two hundred and forty-six gift
  cards have been purchased. The buy one get one free promotion will
  continue until the money runs out. Nevertheless, community members can
  continue to purchase the gift card.

  Vice Chair Varas asked if the program is funded through the ARPA
  Funds.

  Ms. Mares responded to Vice Chair Varas, stating that the American
  Rescue Plan Act funds the program.

  19
 Board Member Lucero questioned if the local businesses would have to
repay an amount for the promotion that is being given.

Ms. Mares explained that the City appropriated those funds for the
program. Business owners participating in the gift card program would not
have to repay. It is free to be a part of the program.

Vice Chair Varas shares his excitement about the program and how it will
help local businesses. He notes that eight of the twenty merchants on the
list are merchants on the boulevard. He continued by asking Ms. Maras if
this program would continue to run once the ARPA Funds are depleted.

Ms. Mares explained that once funds are depleted, it must be presented to
the council to discuss if more funding is needed for the program.

Vice Chair Varas asked if the gift card grants services from the businesses.

Ms. Mares said yes, the gift card grants the services from the business.

Vice Chair Varas continued by asking what would be the total amount to
continue the program once the funds are depleted.

Ms. Mares, at the time, did not have the information. However, she did
mention that residents and the Board could find all information regarding
the program on the agenda bill.

Board Member Masushige wanted clarification on what businesses were a
part of the gift card program.

Ms. Mares reassured her that all businesses on the gift card program are in
the city of South Gate but do not include chain restaurants or large
corporations such as TGIF Fridays.

Board Member Masushige asked if Tweedy Mile had participated in the
program.

Ms. Mares stated that Tweedy Mile is not a part of this program.

Board Member Masushige asked if there could be more advertisements for
the program.

Ms. Mares explained that the city is in the process of promoting the
program.

Vice Chair Varas suggested that the program should be promoted more on
the boulevard.

  Page 2 of 7

  20
   Board Member Masushige gave credit to the city for the signs they have
  made in the past to promote local businesses. She asked if it was possible
  to do this for the gift card program.

  Vice Chair Varas asked for any other comments from his fellow
  colleagues. He asked to make a motion.

  Board Member Masushige agreed to pass the motion.

  Vice Chair Varas asked if there was a limit to the amount of gift cards a
  person can buy.

  Ms. Mares explained that there is currently a limit of two gift cards per
  person.

  City Clerk Glaze asked how much revenue the program has created or
  how many gift cards have been purchased.

  As of that date, Ms. Mares explained that two hundred and thirty gift cards
  were purchased. She encouraged the Board and community members to
  participate in the gift card program.

BID FUNDING FOR FISCAL
YEAR 2022/23 BUDGET  The Tweedy Mile Advisory Board reviewed, discussed, and approved the
  BID funding request received for marketing services.

  Ms. Mares briefly spoke about the BID funding request for marketing
  services. She introduced Ryder Smith, who has worked in other cities, such
  as the City of Paramount, on their website.
  Mr. Smith shares some of his goals for the website and is more than willing
  to share and answer questions regarding the website.
  Vice Chair Varas thanked Ms. Mares for her presentation. He asked if there
  was also going to be an online social media presence for it.
  Ms. Mares explained that, currently, that is not in the works. However, the
  new website will be able to bring out more advertisements.
  Vice Chair Varas was hoping that they could review the forty-thousand-
  dollar budget. He wanted to discuss the reimbursement. He noted that it
  would be about ten percent. But he wanted to know the specifics. His
  concern is that they are able to cover any future expenses.
  Mr. Smith explains that the ten percent reimbursement is only applicable
  when the company is asked to put funds into printing or digital
  advertisement. If someone else is paying the expenses, then there is no fee.
  If the city credit card is used, then the reimbursement would not need to

  Page 3 of 7

  21
   take place, saving about thirteen hundred dollars on the budget. In regard to
  the website hosting, it is an annual fee.
  Vice Chair Varas thanked Mr. Smith for providing more information and
  continued by taking comments from the audience.

COMMENTS FROM
THE AUDIENCE  Resident Jovanna Laborin stated the importance of promoting the business
  on Tweedy Mile. She mentioned that she had a few concerns regarding the
  budget presented. She was under the impression that the city funds
  Tweedy Mile; however, the association takes a membership fee from the
  business on the mile. She asked if implementing this budget would
  promote all businesses on the Tweedy Mile. She stated that not all
  businesses on the mile are aware of what it truly means to be a part of the
  association.

4
COMMENTS FROM
BOARD MEMBERS  Ms. Mares responded to Ms. Laborin’s response and reassured her that the
  city does not fund the association. The Tweedy Mile Advisory Board is the
  one that approves the budget and allocates the funds. The item being
  presented, if approved, would be used to help every business on the mile.

  Vice Chair Varas asked if the website domain would have an option to
  have some Spanish translation.
  Ryder Smith explained that the website will have the option to translate to
  Spanish if needed.
  Vice Chair Varas asked Ms. Mares if it was possible to continue and
  possibly add the digital class to the budget to continue to assist business
  owners with the transition to online marketing. He notes the importance of
  continuing to educate the local businesses on promoting their business
  with the new technological advances. He also wanted to know if it would
  be presented to the Board once the website domain is established.
  Ms. Mares noted that it is possible to provide updates, but they will occur
  during the monthly meetings. She does explain that this process may
  prolong the process. She agrees and hopes to continue the digital classes.
  Vice Chair Varas asked if the digital class advertising campaign was only
  used to promote the gift card program.
  Ms. Mares explained that the campaign itself is separate from the gift card
  program simply because the city has its own funding for the program.
  Vice Chair Varas continues by explaining that the association has the
  ability to choose what it is funded for.

  22
 Mr. Smith suggested the association should spend $10,000 dollars on the
digital advertising campaign as opposed to the $13,000 that is being
presented. Saving the association $3,000 for the classes. He also
mentioned that advertising less may also help the association save funding
for other projects.
Ms. Mares agrees with Mr. Smith. For the next budget, we can always

Ms. Mares advised that Vice Chair Varas lower the advertising spending to

Vice Chair Varas recommends going along with Mr. Smith.

Board Member Lucero explained that word of mouth helped her during

Board Member Lucero asked if the business owners and merchants were

 Vice Chair Varas reassured her that the association is determined to better

Ms. Mares wanted to clarify that the Board did approve the $40,000 for
the budget. It was noted that some of the funding will be allocated for
marketing services.
Vice Chair Varas wanted to inquire about more information regarding
something Mr. Bash mentioned. He asked if the association could share
videos to promote.
Ms. Mares explained that videos can be shared. The Tweedy Mile
Association is a non-profit; they could also use the video to promote.
Vice Chair Varas stresses the fact that this is the association’s opportunity

Board Member Lucero asked if Vice Chair Varas could break down the
$40,000. She wanted to ensure that all businesses on the mile would

Vice Chair Varas explained that the funding for the advertisement would

would spark the viewer’s interest in visiting the boulevard. He also wanted
to explain that the Tweedy Advisory Board used to give funding to the

Ms. Mares wanted to add that the proposal was an engagement for the

Vice Chair Varas asked if there would be multiple websites or just one.
Mr. Smith responded to Vice Chair Varas, stating it would be one website.
He clarified that if the merchants wanted to skip out on the new website
and use the existing one that is out there currently, highlighting the non-

Vice Chair Varas wanted to know more about the process by which the
website would be done. He also wanted to know the process of payment
for the website. He also mentioned that he hoped that could have a staff
report on the website's process and when it will launch.
Ms. Mares explained that the company will invoice the city until they
deliver the completed website. The company will collaborate with the
board, association, and merchant to create this website to ensure everyone

  24
   gets what they want. The company that will be contracted has worked with
  other cities, such as the city of Paramount, with their online presence. She

  Vice Chair Varas made a motion to approve the website and advertisement
  not to exceed the $40,000 budget and noted that the association does not
  have control over the advisory board. He also asked if it was possible to
  have a breakdown of the cost of the digital basic class so it can be
  discussed in the next budget meeting.
  Ms. Mares suggested that if $4,500 is taken out of the advisement fees, it

  Vice Chair Varas explained that he believed it was best not to change the
  current budget and where the funding is being allocated because there is
  no guarantee that business owners will take the course if funded. He

  Ms. Maras said that she would take note of Vice Chair Varas's request.
  Board Member Lucero encouraged the local business owners on the
  boulevard to participate in the meetings.

UPDATE ON THE
MARKETING SERVICES  The Tweedy Mile Advisory Board received and filed the City's update on
  the marketing services for the Tweedy Mile Business Improvement
  District (“Tweedy Mile”) by motion of Chair Varas and seconded by Vice
  Chair Masushige.

  ROLL CALL: Board Member Lucero, yes; Board Member Montes, yes;
  Board Member Zamudio, absent; Vice Chair Masushige, yes; Chair Varas,
  yes.

  Ms. Hernandez stated that in March the Board approved $40,000 for
  marketing services with Tripepi Smith and the vision was to create long
  term assets to drive interest to this business improvement district known as
  Tweedy Mile.

  Ms. Hernandez stated that Amy Conrad from Tripepi Smith is online, and
  she will share how this campaign was created.

  Amy Conrad, Director with Tripepi Smith. They are a marketing, public
  affairs, and technology firm. She and Ms. Hernandez visited several
  businesses on Tweedy Mile. She stated Ms. Hernandez will be showing a
  video of the Tweedy Mile. There will be additional campaign for
  Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.

  Ms. Conrad stated the Tweedy Mile logo reflects the history of the area
  and utilizes current images and themes of the city.

  Ms. Hernandez stated that the website that explores tweedymile.org is now
  live. She also mentioned exploretweedymile.com. She showed a small
  video called “This is Tweedy” to the Board Members.

 1
UPDATE ON THE
MARKETING SERVICES
CONT’D  Chair Varas thanked Ms. Hernandez and Ms. Conrad. And, asked if
  anyone in the audience and zoom wished to speak on this item. Seeing no
  one step forward; Chair Varas closed the audience portion.

  Chair Varas asked if any Board Members had any questions or comments.

  Board Member Lucero liked the video but felt there were too many images
  of the street fair. She was wondering if the video was to promote the street
  fair and not the businesses.

  Ms. Conrad stated they wanted to present the video with the events that
  happen in the Tweedy Mile. Not only a place to shop but a place that is
  happening.

  Chair Varas asked if any businesses had any concerns or feedback.

  Ms. Conrad stated that they had a lot of cooperation and support from all
  the businesses that they contacted.

  Chair Varas liked the video and asked how the businesses were chosen to
  be on the video.

  Ms. Conrad stated it was a randomized pick.

  Ms. Hernandez added that from that list were several dine and shop
  options. Several messages were left for businesses and if they heard
  nothing back from the businesses they moved on to the next business.

  Chair Varas felt the Board should have been informed of how the decision
  was made.

  Vice Chair Masushige would like to see more merchants, especially the
  moms and pops businesses in the video.

  Chair Varas asked if there is a Spanish version.

  Ms. Conrad stated that is something to explore.

  Ms. Hernandez stated that is something that can be added to the video and
